title: Para
subtitle: or, Scenes and Adventures on the Banks of the Amazon
summary: John Esaias Warren (1827–1896), a young American, describes a stay at Pará (now Belém) near the mouth of the Amazon, some years before 1851; he does not give the year. He tells of the town, its churches and festivals, the house outside the town where he lived, and the history of the province, with Orellana’s voyage and the insurrection of 1835. He makes excursions by canoe and stays at Caripe, Jungcal, and Cajueiro, where he hunts and sees wild horses, and he ends with a voyage to Vigia. Much of the book is about the forest, its birds, humming birds, monkeys, snakes, and insects, and about the people of the river. The book has no illustrations.
omitted_from_reading: Nothing is left out after the title page.
notes_on_text: The chapters have no titles in the print, only summaries; the entries of the contents here take the first item of each summary.
